name: Swiss Editorial
style: International Typographic Style on warm paper: a visible six-column grid, a huge flush-left Inter Tight headline, a hairline issue numeral, one cobalt disc exactly two columns wide, thin rules and a tabular Category / Date / Source footer.
bestFor: Serious analysis: research findings and their implications, policy and regulation, benchmark audits, 'what this actually means' explainers.

principles.name: Processing fluency (Reber & Schwarz, 1999)
principles.how: Ink on warm paper at about 16:1 contrast, a single grotesk family, and flush-left, ragged-right lines that all start on the same 80 px axis. The headline is auto-fitted as large as its box allows (about 110 px in the sample, up to 200 px for short hooks). Nothing is centred, justified or set in caps, so the claim reads in one pass, and statements that are easy to read are judged more true.

principles.name: Authority (Cialdini, 1984)
principles.how: The card borrows the look of a journal: a serial issue number, ruled sections, an 'In brief' abstract label and a Category / Date / Source table that always says where the claim comes from. That apparatus signals expertise and sourcing before a word of the copy is read, which suits analysis that has to be believed.

principles.name: Aesthetic-usability effect (Kurosu & Kashimura, 1995)
principles.how: A strict, faintly visible six-column grid governs everything. The disc is exactly two columns wide and as tall as the hero band. The numeral's baseline sits on the disc's bottom edge and the 'No.' label on its top edge. Each side label is cap-aligned with the text it introduces. That visible care reads as quality, and well-made design is judged more credible and easier to use.

principles.name: F-shaped scanning (Nielsen, 2006 eye-tracking)
principles.how: Readers sweep across the top, sweep across again lower down, then scan down the left edge. Here the first sweep crosses the masthead and the numeral-and-disc band, and the second, longest sweep is the full-width headline with its cobalt word. Every element after that starts on the left axis (headline lines, 'In brief' + arrow, Category), so the downward scan picks up the context and the source.

hookFormula: [Big share] of [thing people trust] [vanishes / fails / flips] when [small, everyday change]
captionTip: Let the card carry the claim and use the caption for the method: one line on who tested what and how, the key number, one honest caveat, then a question experts will want to answer ('Which benchmark do you still trust?'). Nuance in the caption earns saves and expert replies, and those replies drive reach.

fieldNotes.issue: Shown as a small label plus a big hairline numeral: 'No. 042' becomes 'No.' + '042', 'Issue 7' becomes 'Issue' + '7'. A value without digits ('Special Edition') is set whole and shrinks to fit its four columns. Empty hides it; the disc stays.
fieldNotes.kicker: Shown as the 'Category' value in the footer table.
fieldNotes.source: Shown under the 'Source' label; a leading 'Source:' is stripped automatically.
fieldNotes.layout: If the headline can't hold 88 px with the full hero, the card switches to a compact one-column hero so long copy still gets a large headline.
